classification.difficultyReason: Reverse the first bearing and combine angles across north to establish the supplied 50° result, then use that angle in the explicitly requested cosine rule.

content.prompt: Two geologists on a large flat area drive $20$ km from point $A$ on a bearing of $150^\circ\mathrm{T}$ to point $B$. They then drive $45$ km on a bearing of $20^\circ\mathrm{T}$ to point $C$.

answer.short: The bearing of $A$ from $B$ is $330^\circ\mathrm{T}$, so $\angle ABC=360^\circ-330^\circ+20^\circ=50^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The reverse bearing of $A$ from $B$ is $150^\circ+180^\circ=330^\circ\mathrm{T}$. The angle at $B$ crosses north, so
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=(360^\circ-330^\circ)+20^\circ\\\angle ABC&=50^\circ.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use the cosine rule to find the distance of point $C$ from point $A$, rounded to the nearest kilometre.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=20^2+45^2-2(20)(45)\cos50^\circ\\AC&=\sqrt{20^2+45^2-2(20)(45)\cos50^\circ}\\AC&\approx36\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
The distance is $36$ km to the nearest kilometre.
